$comment: Copy to config/global.json (gitignored) and edit. Every key here is optional; these are the defaults.
$comment_max_reviews: Quota is shared across all repos. Repos are walked in the order they load (alphabetical by filename), so name them to encode priority.
$comment_provider: Which entry from 'providers' below does the reviewing by default. A repository can name a different one in its own config; see config/repos.sample/.

$comment: The CLIs you have installed and signed in. Every one of these is a terminal
coding agent driven as a subprocess — a review runs on whatever subscription
that CLI already has, and this tool never holds an API key.
An entry named after a known type ('claude', 'codex', 'gemini', 'command')
does not need to repeat it. Any other name is a profile and must say what
type it is — useful for having two settings of the same CLI:
You only need entries for CLIs you actually use; the unused ones cost nothing.
Shared by all of them: the prompt goes in on stdin, the working directory is
an empty scratch dir rather than the checkout, GITHUB_TOKEN is stripped from
the environment, and 'extra_args' is appended verbatim so version-specific
flags never need a code change. What differs is in each entry's $caveats.

claude.$comment_model: null uses whatever your CLI defaults to. Set e.g. 'claude-opus-5' or 'claude-sonnet-5' to pin one.
claude.$comment_extra_args: Appended verbatim to every invocation. CLI flags change between versions — run `claude --help` and put anything version-specific here rather than editing Python.
claude.$comment_allowed_tools: Read-only tools so the reviewer can check surrounding code for conventions. Adding Bash, Write, or Edit would give a PR under review the ability to act on this machine. These names are the config's shared vocabulary; other providers translate them, this one passes them through.
$caveats: None worth listing. This is the tightest of the three: it takes an
explicit tool allowlist AND an explicit denylist, so 'may read files, may
not run anything' is a fact about the process rather than a hope about
the model. The other entries are documented against this one.

codex.$comment_model: null uses your codex default. Run `codex --help` for the names it accepts.
$caveats: Run as `codex exec --sandbox read-only`, which cannot write, install, or
reach the network.
1. That sandbox is read-only about WRITING. Within it the model may run
read-only shell commands and may read paths outside the checkout,
including the rest of your home directory. Wider than the allowlist
providers, where the tool list is the boundary.
2. 'allowed_tools' is not read here — there is no tool list to apply it
to. That includes the empty list merge summaries use, so a summary
runs with the same sandbox a review does rather than with nothing.
3. No --append-system-prompt, so your personality is folded into the top
of the user message instead. Same text, different envelope.

gemini.$comment_allowed_tools: Translated to Gemini's own tool names (read_file, glob, search_file_content). Names it does not recognise are passed through, so a Gemini-specific list works too.
$caveats: 1. Writes are blocked by withholding approval, not by dropping the tools.
It runs with --approval-mode default, so a write needs a confirmation
a non-interactive run cannot give and therefore fails. DO NOT put
--approval-mode yolo in extra_args — that is the whole guard.
2. --include-directories grants write access as well as read, which is
why point 1 is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces.
3. No --append-system-prompt; folded into the message, as with codex.

$comment_command_type: The escape hatch. type 'command' runs anything that takes a prompt on stdin
and prints an answer on stdout, with extra_args as the whole command line:
Caveat, and it is the whole caveat: nothing here can restrict what that
command does. No allowlist, no denylist, no sandbox — it gets whatever it
gives itself. Point it at something read-only and treat it as a program you

merge_summary.$comment: The one-line 'what changed' on the Summary tab. Written once per merged pull request and kept, so this is the cheapest call the tool makes: a few hundred lines of metadata, no tools, no checkout. Set false to keep the merge record but leave the descriptions blank.
merge_summary.$comment_provider: null means summaries run on whatever provider reviews that repository. Name one here to send every summary somewhere else — worth it if you keep a cheaper CLI around, since this is a summarising job, not a judging one. Setting this drops any per-repo model pin, which belongs to a different provider.
merge_summary.$comment_model: null reuses the provider's model. Worth pointing at a smaller model than the reviewer uses.
merge_summary.$comment_max_per_tick: Cap on retries per repository per tick, for merges whose first summary call failed. New merges are always summarised as they are found.
merge_summary.$comment_max_tries: After this many failed attempts the description falls back to our own review summary, so a missing CLI cannot buy a failed subprocess every tick forever.

notifications.$comment: macOS only. Set enabled=false to silence, or swap in terminal-notifier / a shell script that takes --title and --message.

logging.$comment: Logs record repo, PR number, decision, and token counts. Prompt and diff bodies are written only when you pass --debug, and then only to the state dir.
